'''Eudóxia Maria Froehlich''' (21 October 1928 – 26 September 2015) was a Brazilian [[zoology|zoologist]].

==Life==
Born in 1928, Eudóxia Maria de Oliveira Pinto was the daughter of Alice Alves de Camargo and the ornithologist [[Olivério Pinto|Olivério Mário de Oliveira Pinto]]. Since she was a child, her parents used to take her and her siblings to the wooded areas near [[São Paulo]], which helped her to become interested in zoology, especially small animals.<ref name="EudoxiaInterview">Carbayo, F. (2013) "Vida de Zoólogo: Eudóxia Maria Froehlich." ''Informativo da Sociedade Brasileira de Zoologia'' '''106''': 7–10.</ref>

After finishing High School, she spent six months in [[Rio de Janeiro]] with an uncle who was a physician and returned home interested in studying [[medicine]]. Her father did not approve the idea, considering it an inappropriate career for a woman, and suggested her to study [[natural history]] and so she did.<ref name="EudoxiaInterview" /> During this time she became engaged to [[Claudio Gilberto Froehlich]], one of her colleagues.

In 1951 she and Froehlich started their doctoral studies at the [[Universidade de São Paulo]] together, having [[Ernst Marcus (zoologist)|Ernst Marcus]] as their advisor. Marcus suggested that they should work on the taxonomy of [[Geoplanidae|land planarians]], since it was a poorly studied but highly diverse group in the region.<ref name="EudoxiaInterview" />

She continued her studies with land planarians until 1978 and then changed her attention to [[Arachnida|arachnids]]. She retired in 1988, but continued her work as an emerita professor, being active until her death in 2015.{{citation needed|date=February 2017}}

== Homages ==
The land planarian genus ''[[Eudoxiatopoplana]]'', as well as the species ''[[Obama eudoxiae]]'', ''[[Obama eudoximariae]]'' and ''[[Notogynaphallia froehlichae]]'', were named after her.<ref name="Winsor2009">{{cite journal | last1 = Winsor | first1 = L. | year = 2009 | title = A new subfamily, new genus and new species of terrestrial flatworm (Platyhelminthes: Tricladida: Geoplanidae) from Stewart Island, New Zealand | journal = Tuhinga: Records of the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa | volume = 20 | pages = 23–32 | url = https://www.tepapa.govt.nz/sites/default/files/tuhinga.20.2009.pt3_.p23-32.winsor.pdf | archive-date = 2019-01-30 | access-date = 2017-02-20 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190130225733/https://www.tepapa.govt.nz/sites/default/files/tuhinga.20.2009.pt3_.p23-32.winsor.pdf | url-status = dead }} {{open access}}</ref><ref name="Ogren1990">{{cite journal | last1 = Ogren | first1 = Robert E. | last2 = Kawakatsu | first2 = Masaharu | title = Index to the species of the family Geoplanidae (Turbellaria, Tricladida, Terricola) Part I: Geoplaninae | journal = The Bulletin of Fuji Women's College |series=Series 2 | volume = 28 | year = 1990 | pages = 79–166 | url = http://ci.nii.ac.jp/naid/110008426079/en}} {{Open access}}</ref>
